forms_forms.description: Create, read, update, duplicate, convert and delete forms, and inspect their fields, shortcodes, embedding pages and edit history.

forms_submissions.description: Read and manage form submissions (entries): filters, notes, logs, statuses, favorites, bulk actions, and the public submission endpoint.

forms_settings.description: Per-form settings: general options, confirmations, style customizer, entry columns, conversational design, and style presets.

forms_integrations.description: Connect forms to third-party services: global integration credentials and per-form integration feeds.

forms_reports.description: Read-only analytics for forms: submission counts, completion rates, revenue, payment types, heatmaps and top-performing forms.

forms_admin.description: Site-level Fluent Forms administration: global settings, licensing, managers and role capabilities.
forms_admin.note: The license endpoints require Fluent Forms Pro.

forms_utilities.description: Maintenance and helper operations: system logs, global search, admin notices, plugin install helpers, and the MCP adapter settings.

form-submit/submit-form.summary: Submit a Form Entry (public — fires notifications, integrations and payments)
form-submit/submit-form.bodyNote: Public endpoint: this creates a REAL submission as an end user would, firing email notifications, integration feeds and payment processing. Body shape: {"form_id": <id>, "data": "<url-encoded field=value pairs>"} — the same payload the front-end form posts.

suggested-plugins/install-plugin.bodyNote: Installs an ARBITRARY plugin from wordpress.org by slug ({"plugin_slug": "..."}) — the endpoint does not restrict the slug to Fluent Forms' suggestions.

suggested-plugins/activate-plugin.bodyNote: Activates any installed plugin by slug ({"plugin_slug": "..."}) — i.e. starts executing its code on the site.

integrations/save-form-integration.bodyNote: Body shape: {"integration_name": "<registered slug>", "integration": {"name": "<feed name>", "enabled": true, "list_id": …, "merge_fields"/other per-integration fields…, "conditionals": {"status": false, "type": "all", "conditions": []}}, "integration_id": <existing feed id to update, omit to create>}. integration_name MUST be one of the slugs in forms_integrations_list's available_integrations (e.g. "fluentcrm", "fluent_support", "fluent_community", "wp_social_ninja" — note the inconsistent underscores): Fluent Forms stores the feed under "<integration_name>_feeds" without checking the name, so a wrong slug saves a row the submission processor never runs. This tool refuses unregistered names before writing and returns the feed as Fluent Forms lists it (`stored`) after. Status-only toggle: {"integration_id": <id>, "status": false} with no "integration". Read an existing feed first with forms_integrations_get {query: {integration_id, integration_name}} and mirror its shape.

integrations/get-form-integration.bodyNote: Pass query: {"integration_id": <feed id>, "integration_name": "<slug>"} — both come from forms_integrations_list (feed id, and provider minus the "_feeds" suffix). Without integration_id it returns that integration's default settings template, which is the shape to send to forms_integrations_save.

integrations/delete-form-integration.bodyNote: Pass query: {"integration_id": <feed id>} (from forms_integrations_list). The delete is scoped to form_id.

integrations/list-form-integrations.summary: List Form Integration Feeds (with available integration slugs)
